title: Shared definitions
description: Definitions shared by every Periscope data contract. Not an entity: nothing validates against this file directly. Design rules that hold across all schemas: every object is closed (additionalProperties false); no schema declares a number, integer or boolean anywhere, so no field can carry a score, weight, likelihood, rank or flag; identifiers are built from dates and word slugs, never from sequence numbers, so no identifier can encode an order of importance. The .invalid host in every $id is reserved by RFC 2606 and can never be fetched.

label.description: The honesty vocabulary from CLAUDE.md invariant 5, six values since DM-1 (4 Oct 2026). Semantics under DM-2: the label states origin. real = a published, verifiable item, or a statement about the demo that a named test verifies; ai-generated = text written offline by an agent; fictional = content about the invented Tracewell team; replay = the decision log's entries and past judgements; yours = text and choices the viewer enters in this tab; frozen = an assembled container whose parts carry their own labels (in this build, the weekly brief only). Must equal LABELS in assets/js/contracts/vocabulary.js (M1-U5).

generatedLabel.description: The label of a fixture entity written offline by an agent. Under DM-2 the label states origin, so it is fixed: ai-generated, never frozen, real or fictional.

lens.description: The three rival lenses. Peers: the enumeration order here is alphabetical and carries no meaning. The order the viewer sees is drawn at random per trend per page load (Q-2, docs/03-architecture.md section 7.3).

producer.description: Who produced an entity. Pipeline agents by their agent name; architect is the build agent that drafts the governance argument from the Scout's frozen source list (Q-5); persona-researcher is the Cowork Persona and Brief Researcher; project-author is a human author of the project; viewer is the person using the demo, in-session only.

practiceKey.description: The foresight practices that each receive a maturity level (D-1): the three methods R2 names, in the order R2 names them. The list is to be confirmed against the thesis by the Verifier (open item O-3). Must equal PRACTICE_KEYS in vocabulary.js (M1-U5).

dateTime.description: Instant in UTC as produced by Date.prototype.toISOString(). Used only for in-session records, to make the order of intuition, reveal, commit and scenario checkable.

httpsUrl.description: An absolute https URL to a public source. Rendered only as an <a href> the viewer chooses to follow; never loaded by the demo.

text.description: Non-empty prose containing at least one non-whitespace character.

oneLine.description: A single line of prose, at most 200 characters, with at least one non-whitespace character.

questionText.description: A question, not advice: non-empty and ending with a question mark.

slug.description: Lower-case word segments joined by hyphens. Each segment starts with a letter, so a slug cannot be a bare sequence number.

signalId.description: sig-<publication date>-<slug>. The date part must equal provenance.publishedOn (checked by M3-U5).

readingId.description: reading-<trend slug>-<lens>. M1-U9 checks that the suffix equals the reading's lens and the middle equals its trend's slug.

conversationId.description: conversation-<trend slug>. M1-U9 checks that the slug equals its trend's slug.

questionId.description: Unique across every Interrogation and every ConversationQuestions set (M4-U8).

entryId.description: replay-<publication date of the earliest original signal>-<slug>.

testId.description: Identifier of a unit test in docs/04-module-design.md (for example M10-U1) or of an invariant audit in docs/test-plan.md (AUDIT-1 to AUDIT-6).

role.description: R7, designed for and not built. The role of the team member a judgement belongs to, as a slug (for example ceo, cto). Absent means the sole founder: a single-founder team is the same model with the field omitted. No fixture in this build populates it and no UI code reads it.

generatedText.description: A part of a composite entity that was written offline by an agent while the entity as a whole has another origin (DM-2, per-part labels): a real signal's English summary and relevance note, a replay outcome's paraphrase, a calibration note (DM-10), a next-level description. The label is fixed to ai-generated.

sourceRef.description: A dated citation for one factual claim (NF2). All four core fields are required.

reportCitation.description: A citation of a report at a specific page (F3, K-2): the title is required so the report is named, and the page is a string such as '9' or '9-11'. The page is text, not a number, so that the no-number rule holds without exception; it locates a claim and orders nothing.

provenance.description: Where an entity came from. The four external-source fields travel together: all four are set when the entity as a whole is a real, published item, and all four are null when it was generated or authored, in which case the claims inside it carry their own sourceRef (DM-3, ratified 4 Oct 2026). Null here is a statement ('there is no external source for this entity as a whole'), not an omission. producedBy, producedOn and frozenOn record who made it, when, and when it was frozen at G3.

frozenProvenance.description: Provenance of a fixture: produced offline by an agent or a project author on a known date, and frozen at G3. Never produced by the viewer.

publishedProvenance.description: Provenance of a fixture that is itself a real, published item: the external-source fields must be set.

sessionProvenance.description: Provenance of a record the viewer creates in the browser tab (Judgement, ScenarioRecord). No external source, produced by the viewer alone, never frozen, never stored.
